papers.title: Discourse Diversity in Multi-Turn Empathic Dialogue

training_data.name: filtered WildChat and SENSE-7 emotional-support conversations
training_data.quote: Our training data comes from two complementary sources of real user–LLM interactions: WildChat (Zhao et al., 2024), a large-scale corpus of ChatGPT conversations spanning diverse topics, and SENSE-7 (Suh et al., 2026), a corpus of emotionally supportive dialogues annotated with perceived empathy ratings. From both corpora, we retain only English-language conversations with at least 3 turns. The resulting dataset contains 322 multi-turn emotional-support conversations totaling 1,719 supporter turns.

training_data.name: WildChat
training_data.quote: WildChat is a collection of 1 million conversations between human users and ChatGPT. Language(s) (NLP): multi-lingual.

training_data.name: SENSE-7
training_data.quote: The SENSE-7 subset of our training data (Suh et al., 2026) includes post-task user ratings on four satisfaction dimensions. For each of the 69 SENSE-7 conversations, we compute the average tactic stickiness.

source_claims.quote: We evaluate Mint on two base policy models, Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B (Yang et al., 2025). Training is implemented in VERL (Sheng et al., 2025) with GRPO.
MINT Qwen3 4B | hongli-zhan/MINT-empathy-Qwen3-4B | Released 4B MINT checkpoint

description.text:
This model is the Q + D_KL MINT checkpoint fine-tuned from Qwen/Qwen3-4B for multi-turn empathic dialogue.

MINT, short for Multi-turn Inter-tactic Novelty Training, is a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes empathic response quality together with cross-turn discourse-move novelty. In the paper, this checkpoint is the best overall released MINT model, delivering the strongest joint tradeoff between empathy quality and reduced cross-turn tactic repetition.

output_type.quote: This model is the Q + D_KL MINT checkpoint fine-tuned from Qwen/Qwen3-4B for multi-turn empathic dialogue.

use_claim.quote: This model is intended for research on empathic dialogue, discourse diversity, and supportive response generation.

warning.quote: It is a research artifact, not a therapy system, and it was evaluated on fixed gold-history conversation contexts rather than fully interactive free-running conversations.

serving.notes: The card's usage example loads AutoModelForCausalLM and does not pass an image or audio input. tokenizer_config.json has no chat_template key; the Hub API returns the chat_template.jinja text, and that template adds a system turn only when the first message is already a system message. config.json max_position_embeddings is 40960; tokenizer model_max_length is 131072. The paper states 3 epochs, learning rate 1e-6, and batch size 24 prompts with 8 rollouts, for the Qwen3-4B MINT runs. The training script sets lora_rank=0 and its default MODEL_PATH is Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B. The weight upload commit is titled Upload MINT Q+D_KL Qwen3-4B (global_step_180). The paper HTML does not print the repository id. The 4B Q + D_KL row in the paper is aggregate empathy 4.67 and tactic stickiness 0.42, the same numbers as the card.

evaluation_reported.text: On the Lend-an-Ear test set reported in the paper, which contains 315 supporter turns across 50 conversations: aggregate empathy improves from 3.75 to 4.67 relative to the vanilla Qwen3-4B baseline, and tactic stickiness decreases from 0.57 to 0.42.

discrepancies: The card states GRPO and the parent Qwen/Qwen3-4B. It does not name WildChat or SENSE-7. The paper's training-data section names both, which matches the inventory row. The training set used is a filtered mix of 322 English conversations, not the full corpora.
